author: sonnet
label: c2-seed-sonnet-01
changes: Added the three sync triggers and push-then-pull order to the notes (Q1).
Spelled out the push contents, batch limit of 100 and per-change result (Q2, Q8).
Defined the version check and where starting versions come from (Q3).
Stated that the server creates the conflict copy and what B sees after the next pull (Q4).
Explained processed change IDs and replay returning the stored result (Q5).
Added a rule for edits made while a change is in flight, with the starting version updated from the result (Q6).
Defined the cursor, page limit of 500 and when it advances (Q7).
Added failure handling for dropped pushes and pulls, plus the one open question about re-editing after a conflict (Q8).
Made the diagram arrows carry the key data; kept the intent unchanged.
Added New notes line: starting version 0 for a note with no server version, server treats unknown note ID as version 0 (Q12).
Result now says the phone sets local version to the new version on accepted, so its own log entry is ignored (Q9).
Conflict copy now gives the conflict note a new ID, version 1, ordinary-note status, and says what B sees before and if the pull fails (Q10, Q11).
Changes in flight now distinguishes accepted (take new version) from conflict (keep old starting version) (Q13); open questions extended.
Push now says the next batch waits for the previous results; Retries covers an edit made meanwhile (Q14).
Added Server errors line: stop at first unexpected error, return partial results, phone removes only those (Q15); open question added for a change that always errors.
Added a Versions line with a worked example (3 vs 4) so what each phone holds and why B loses is explicit (Q16).
Added Applying an entry: create unknown notes, replace local copy only when entry version is newer (Q17, Q20).
Decided that a pull overwrites local text while a queued change stays and later conflicts into a conflict note, so nothing is lost (Q18).
Said collapsing only applies to unsent changes and that a new change after a frozen one gets its own change ID (Q19).
Added a Log entries line listing what an entry contains and that the conflict note is an ordinary entry (Q20).
Said a no-response push abandons the sync without pulling, and that a 60 second tick is skipped while a sync is running (Q21).
Said a new phone pulls from cursor 0, and added an open question that the log is never trimmed (Q22).
Replaced the one-line summary with a three-sentence summary that also says how the app works today (local-only SQLite, no server).
Added a Terms section defining outbox, change, starting version, version, change log, cursor, processed change IDs and conflict note in one line each.
Moved the version example under the diagram as a note instead of a bullet inside the rules.

Merged the many separate bullets (Triggers, Edits, New notes, Push, Result, Versions, Version check, Conflict copy, Retries, Changes in flight, Log entries, Applying an entry, Cursor, Failure) into seven numbered steps in execution order, each naming actor and what it does.
Merged Version check, Conflict copy, and the server half of Retries into step 4. Moved Retries and the stored-result rule so the stored result is described once.
Merged Server errors, Retries-on-lost-response, Failure and the pull-failure text into one failure table; removed repeated statements that nothing is lost.
Folded the Log entries field list into the Terms definition of change log, and the Versions line into the starting version term plus the example.
Cut the repeated explanation that the new phone pulls everything (kept once in step 6) and the duplicate wording about B's pull failure.

Kept all stated limits and rules: 100 changes per push, 500 entries per page, 60 second timer with tick skip, collapse keeping original starting version, version up by one, conflict note title and version 1, out of scope list, and the three open questions.
Added no new mechanisms and made no changes to the plan's behavior.
